Observation: No visible focus indicator appears on links, buttons, or fields when navigating by keyboard; suppressed globally in the CSS reset.
Impact: Keyboard-only users cannot tell where they are on the page, making the site difficult or impossible to navigate without a mouse.
Recommendation: Restore visible focus states site-wide as part of the global stylesheet.
At a Glance: Patients who navigate by keyboard can't reliably tell where they are on any page of the site, which is both a real barrier and a compliance risk.
Evidence: https://example-site.com/, /book, /reset-password, /insurance-faq, /contact; global.css rule `*:focus { outline: none }`; tabbed through each page, no focus ring on a, button, input
Instances: 5 pages: Homepage, Appointment Booking, Password Reset, Insurance FAQ, Contact (shared stylesheet)

Location: Appointment Booking page, Confirm Appointment button
Observation: Confirm button is a styled div with a click handler; no accessible name or role.
Impact: Screen reader users hear nothing identifying the button's purpose.
Recommendation: Use a native button element or add role and aria-label.
At a Glance: Screen reader users can't tell what the appointment booking submit button does before activating it.
